task: Predict disease-specific survival in colorectal adenocarcinoma using four ordered time bins with censored versus event status. Classes represent early to late follow-up intervals, split by whether disease-specific death occurred. H&E features linked to worse disease-specific outcome include high-grade histology, tumor budding, lymphovascular invasion, infiltrative growth, and deep wall penetration.

classes.0: Earliest time bin, censored — short disease-specific follow-up without disease-specific death.
classes.1: Second time bin, censored — intermediate-early follow-up without disease-specific death.
classes.2: Third time bin, censored — intermediate-late follow-up without disease-specific death.
classes.3: Fourth time bin, censored — longest follow-up without disease-specific death.
classes.4: Earliest time bin, event — disease-specific death occurred early, consistent with aggressive colorectal adenocarcinoma morphology.
classes.5: Second time bin, event — disease-specific death occurred at an intermediate-early interval.
classes.6: Third time bin, event — disease-specific death occurred at an intermediate-late interval.
classes.7: Fourth time bin, event — disease-specific death occurred late after prolonged follow-up.
